title: Priority Factor Matrix (PFM) — workload-aware roadmap scoring
creator: Ethan Liu
description: Introduce the Priority Factor Matrix (PFM), a hybrid prioritization rubric designed for Redwood Inference roadmap decisions. PFM extends RICE by explicitly folding in workload characteristics (latency sensitivity, token-volume elasticity), per-customer revenue exposure, and rollout risk. The aim is to produce a single, interpretable score that helps product, engineering, and design choose initiatives that balance customer value, operational cost, and reliability trade-offs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
scoring_guide:
Overview: PFM_score = Norm(RICE) * ElasticityFactor * RevenueWeight * (1 - RiskAdj).
Steps: 1) Compute base RICE (Reach * Impact * Confidence / Effort). 2) Normalize RICE to 0..1 across candidate set. 3) ElasticityFactor (0.5..1.5): derived from measured token-volume elasticity and latency-sensitivity bucket (batch-friendly workloads get >1). 4) RevenueWeight (0.5..2.0): higher for initiatives tied to top 10% of ARR or strategic enterprise logos. 5) RiskAdj (0..0.4): technical complexity, cross-team dependencies, regulatory constraints.
Interpretation: higher PFM_score indicates high priority. Use score bands (>=0.75: Target for next cycle; 0.5-0.75: Candidate; <0.5: Backlog).
sample_calculation: Example: feature X increases throughput for embeddings-heavy routes. RICE base = 160. Normalized RICE = 0.86. ElasticityFactor = 1.25 (batching + caching hit expected). RevenueWeight = 1.4 (affects top enterprise customers). RiskAdj = 0.08 (minor infra changes). PFM_score = 0.86 * 1.25 * 1.4 * (1 - 0.08) = 1.38 -> normalized band -> Target for next cycle. (We then compare across candidates and apply capacity constraints.)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Discovery): instrument token-volume & latency buckets for top routes and collect 8 weeks of telemetry (owners: ENG-observability, PM). Phase 2 (Scoring and calibration): run PFM across current initiatives; workshop with Eng/Design to validate ElasticityFactor mappings. Phase 3 (Pilot): select 2 PFM-high projects for a canary quarter with embedded evals and cost monitoring. Phase 4 (Operationalize): embed PFM scoring into quarterly planning doc and add a lightweight scoring form in Confluence and the roadmap spreadsheet.

comments: 2025-02-13 — PM sync: proposed PFM to exec; positive reception. Request from infra for clearer definition of ElasticityFactor sources (telemetry vs heuristic).

2025-02-20 — ENG feedback (Priya R.): suggested mapping latency-sensitivity using 95th pct latency and tail latency tolerance per customer tier; proposed adding a separate 'SLA exposure' multiplier. We'll model SLA exposure as part of RiskAdj for now to keep score compact.

2025-02-24 — Design review (Omar B.): asked to include UX complexity as part of RiskAdj and surface qualitative trade-offs in roadmap slides. Agreed to add a short 'UX effort note' in the scoring template.

2025-02-28 — PM update: ran PFM on current backlog (42 initiatives). Initial normalization skewed by one outlier (massive long-term platform rewrite). Decided to use percentile-based normalization (5th-95th) to avoid outlier distortion.
2025-03-01 — ENG (Sanjay) blocked on observability instrumentation; created ENG-9182 for telemetry collection. Without this, ElasticityFactor will be heuristic and flagged as low confidence.

2025-03-03 — Calibration workshop notes: lowered default RiskAdj for infra-only changes if covered by existing dedicated capacity budget; agreed to revisit RevenueWeight thresholds after revenue owner input (scheduled 2025-03-11).
